rationale: Taxonomy hard-codes project.member_spend_enforcement.updated as "Settings" instead of "Budget", failing AC17's requirement that Budget include the enforcement event (CR-002, critical) — the diff's own tests assert the wrong behavior. Standards audit blocks on two non-ticket-prefixed commit subjects (CR-005) and a bare list[dict] typing violation (CR-001); a pre-existing test assertion on get_domain_mapping's entity_types was silently deleted (CR-004), and the new trail endpoint's auth-dependency wiring has no HTTP-level test unlike its metadata sibling (CR-003). One pre-existing find_all pagination tie-break gap was deferred as out of scope; 8 other candidates (unknown-event_type KeyError risk, invalid-category silent empty set, VARCHAR(255) truncation risk, a false-positive NameError claim, naive-datetime comparison, missing project-existence check, pagination page-number math, and unguarded ais_admin DB call) were verified against source and dismissed as unreachable, already consistent with established codebase conventions, or mathematically correct.

findings.title: Bare list[dict] typing on metadata field
findings.problem: ActivityEventProjectMetadata.event_types is declared as bare list[dict] instead of a parameterized generic or dedicated model, so the {event_type, label, category} shape is enforced only by convention in get_project_event_metadata.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality standard is violated in new code; a future caller populating this field with a different shape would not be caught by schema validation, and the standards audit already flags this as a blocking finding.
findings.recommendation: Declare the field as list[dict[str, str]] or, preferably, a dedicated Pydantic model for the event_type/label/category triple.

findings.title: Enforcement event miscategorized as Settings
findings.problem: EVENT_TAXONOMY maps project.member_spend_enforcement.updated to category "Settings" instead of "Budget", contradicting the spec's explicit instruction that Budget must include every BudgetManagementEvent type plus the new member-spend-enforcement event.
findings.impact: Filtering the project trail by category=["Budget"] excludes the enforcement event, failing AC17 ("Selecting Budget returns budget events and the enforcement event together"). The diff's own tests (test_find_by_project_category_filter_resolves_to_event_types_via_taxonomy and test_member_spend_enforcement_updated_event_constant_exists) assert and lock in the wrong category, so this is a required-criterion failure, not a cosmetic slip.
findings.recommendation: Change the taxonomy entry to ("Member Spend Enforcement Updated", "Budget") and flip the two tests that currently assert "Settings" to assert "Budget".

findings.title: Main trail route's auth wiring has no HTTP-level test
findings.problem: TestListProjectActivityEvents' tests all call list_project_activity_events(...) as a plain Python function with _=None, never through a TestClient, so FastAPI's Depends(project_admin_or_admin_or_maintainer_access) resolution is never exercised for this route; only the /metadata sibling has such a test.
findings.impact: If the dependency is dropped, renamed, or mis-wired on this specific endpoint while the metadata endpoint keeps it, any authenticated user could list another project's full activity trail (including actor_email/actor_display_name/entity_label), and no existing test would catch it.
findings.recommendation: Add a TestClient-based access-control test for GET /v1/projects/{project_name}/activity-events mirroring TestGetProjectActivityEventsMetadataAccessControl, asserting a non-project-admin gets 403 and list_project_events is never called.

findings.title: Deleted coverage for get_domain_mapping entity_types
findings.problem: The pre-existing assertion assert result['user_management'].entity_types == ['user'] in test_get_domain_mapping_groups_by_domain was deleted with no replacement and no stated reason, in a diff whose purpose is adding get_distinct_event_types_by_project coverage.
findings.impact: Silent regression-coverage loss for get_domain_mapping's entity_types field, which is unrelated to this diff's stated scope; a future regression in that field would go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Restore the deleted assertion alongside the new test_get_distinct_event_types_by_project_returns_event_types test.

findings.title: Two commits use non-ticket commit-message prefix
findings.problem: Commits 2b6f83598 ("project-scoped-activity-trail: commit remaining planning artifacts and doctor cache refresh") and 3b46a8bd5 ("project-scoped-activity-trail: add planning artifacts") use a task-slug prefix instead of the required EPMCDME-####: Description format documented in git-workflow.md.
findings.impact: Breaks the convention used to trace changes to the Jira ticket; this is a documented blocking standard.
findings.recommendation: Reword the two commit subjects (via rebase, if the branch is not yet merged) to start with EPMCDME-14325:.
